newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco millers seek help following liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Morocco millers seek help following liberalisation.

text.p: Morocco's millers on Wednesday said the country would face a food and social crisis if urgent measures were not taken to absorb negative impacts of the cereal sector liberalisation.

"The government, which liberalised the cereal imports in May 1, to comply with the General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs rules, took no measures to help the cereal industry," Ghali Sebti, president of the National Federation of Cereal Activity told Reuters.
Sebti was commenting the results of a the meeting held by the millers association on Tuesday.

He said the government could face a dramatic drop of the country's cereal output, acceleration of urban drift, surge of cereal imports and increase of trade deficit and dependence of Morocco on cereal multinationals.
With an annual turnover of 100 billion dirhams, the cereal sector employs 40 percent of the Moroccan population, Sebti said.
The millers association, which represents the country's 150 enterprises, addressed a letter to the agriculture ministry to drawing attraction to dangers of bankruptcies and closures.
Over a period of 10 years, Morocco has produced 50 percent of its cereal needs but the problem of improving productivity remains, experts said.
"To meet the market increasing demand and compete against foreign products, the domestic cereal industry should be upgraded as soon as possible," Sebti said.
The association said the first impacts of the liberalisation were speculation and a lack of cooordination to supervise the imports.

"In a very good agricultural season and while the demand is very low on the domestic market, the state-run Office National des Cereales et Legumineuses and private traders has already imported 0.6 million tonnes of soft wheat since May 1, 1996," a trader said.
